header.running_head: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Ensures that Jihaad is Waged Against the Murtaddeen and Those Who Refused to Pay Zakaah

blocks.text:
Arab tribes left the fold of Islaam when they said that they would perform salaah without paying zakaah. He narrates further that he then approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Be sympathetic towards the people and show mercy towards them for they are like wild animals." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Whereas I was hopeful of your help, you have come to inform me that you will not render any assistance. While you had been powerful during the Period of Ignorance, have you become weak in Islaam? Why should I sympathise with them using composed verse or concocted magic? Farfetched! Farfetched! Rasulullaah ﷺ has passed away and revelation has stopped. I swear by Allaah that I shall fight them as long as my hand can hold a sword and (if) they refuse to pay even a string (that is due from them as zakaah)."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "I found Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to be more competent and resolute than myself. He trained the people in many matters which made many of my tasks easy when I was appointed as Khalifah." [^1]

Hadhrat Dabba bin Mihsin Anzi narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), "Are you better than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) began to weep and said, "A single night of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a single day of his is better than (the life's deeds of) Umar and the entire family of Umar. Should I not inform you of that night and that day of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)?" When Hadhrat Dabba asked to be informed, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "The night was the night when Rasulullaah ﷺ left the people of Makkah. He left at night and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) followed him." He then proceeded to narrate the incident as reported in the Chapter Concerning Hijrah[^2]. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then continued, "The day of his was when Rasulullaah ﷺ had passed away and many Arab tribes forsook Islaam. While some of them said that they would perform salaah without paying zakaah, others said that they would neither perform salaah nor pay zakaah. I then approached him with the sincere intention of offering good counsel. I said to him, 'O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Be compassionate towards the people..." The rest of the Hadith is similar to the one quoted above. [^3]

Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ had passed away and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) succeeded him, many Arab tribes forsook Islaam. It was then that Hadhrat Umar (RA) approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "O Abu Bakr! How can we fight these people when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'I have been commanded to fight people until they declare 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah'. When someone declares 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah', his property and life is safe from me except by the right of Allaah (a warrant by which his property or life may be taken as a penalty). Thereafter, Allaah shall reckon with him."
Ismaa'ili, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.300).

Under the heading "The Hijrah of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)" and the subheading "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Fears for Rasulullaah ﷺ when they Leave the Cave and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Praises Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)".
Dinowri in his Majaalasah, Abul Hasan bin Bishraan in his Fawaa'id, Bayhaqi in his Dalaa'il and La'lakaai in his Sunnah, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.348).
